official.description_text:
Postdoc in ÄMNESOMRÅDE
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher with an interest in generative AI, machine learning, natural language processing, and human–robot interaction. You will work within a newly awarded project at the
Department of Speech, Music and Hearing
at the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at KTH. TMH is an internationally recognized research environment in speech and language technology, with a particular focus on multimodal interaction with social robots. The newly launched Promobilia-funded project
SAInt
: Situated Agentic Interaction aims to develop and evaluate humanoid assistive robots capable of understanding context, learning through interaction, and providing proactive support. The goal is to contribute to reducing the care gap for older adults and people with special needs. Within the five-year project, the doctoral student will collaborate with researchers and doctoral students at the
Department of Robotics, Perception and Learning
. The overall objective of SAInt is to move beyond traditional robotics for support and assistance, which rely on explicit command structures, and instead develop agentic systems capable of contextual understanding, inferring user goals through natural multimodal communication, and collaborating proactively as an integrated part of everyday activities. Your task is to develop and evaluate a dialogue architecture that moves beyond reactive systems and enables the humanoid robot to understand user goals, actions, ongoing activities, and cognitive states, in order to determine when and how verbal and physical assistance should be provided.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in computer science, machine learning, computational linguistics, robotics, human–computer interaction, or a closely related field. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented experience in experimentally evaluating robots that interact through speech.
Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, PyTorch).
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Previous experience in developing and evaluating robots that interact through speech training is highly meritorious. Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, three years.
A

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in developing and evaluating dialogue architecture for humanoid assistive robots. Role focuses on natural language processing, generative AI, and multimodal interaction to enable context-aware, proactive robot assistance for older adults and people with special needs. Embedded in a 5-year agentic interaction project (SAInt) at KTH's Department of Speech, Music and Hearing.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position involves human–robot interaction, multimodal communication, and context-aware systems—adjacent to human-centred systems design. However, core focus is dialogue architecture, generative AI, and NLP for robot agency, not immersive learning, spatial cognition, or collaborative XR. The 'human' dimension is assistive support/care, not collaborative learning or wayfinding. Social robot interaction is relevant to multiplayer/social immersive systems, but the specific modality (dialogue, speech) and domain (assistive robotics) diverge from immersive spatial environments.

methodological_fit.rationale: Overlap in experimental evaluation (human–robot interaction studies), understanding user goals and contexts, and developing systems that respond to human needs. Researcher has intermediate user-studies and experimental-design skills. However, position emphasizes machine learning (generative AI, NLP, PyTorch), speech processing, and agentic AI systems—not multiplayer mechanics, immersive interface design, or spatial learning outcomes. The evaluation likely focuses on task success, user preference, and safety, not spatial familiarity or real-world transfer.

growth_value.rationale: Would develop deep expertise in generative AI, NLP, dialogue systems, and experimental evaluation of human–AI interaction. Valuable for interdisciplinary HCI research. However, limited upskilling in immersive technologies, spatial design, or collaborative gameplay mechanics. Would broaden understanding of context-aware, adaptive systems but pivot away from XR/VR domain.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong European research institution (Stockholm, Sweden—preferred country). Department of Speech, Music and Hearing is internationally recognized in multimodal interaction. Position is embedded in newly awarded 5-year project (Promobilia-funded, stable). Advisor/group is reputable. However, no explicit connection to immersive systems or XR research. Postdoc is 3-year contract; pathway to next role depends on project evolution. Research culture (robotics, speech, AI) is adjacent to HCI but not core target.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD; researcher has MSc by Research (in progress). Thesis must be completed and degree awarded before employment decision.

Posting states 'Documented experience in experimentally evaluating robots that interact through speech' is required; researcher has no documented experience with robotic systems or speech interaction.
Strong programming skills in Python and PyTorch are required; researcher has beginner-level Python experience only.
Position may require security clearance if classified as 'security-sensitive role' under Swedish Protective Security Act; timeline and eligibility criteria unclear.
risks: Domain pivot: assistive robotics with dialogue focus diverges from immersive collaborative learning systems.
Technology gap: generative AI and NLP are orthogonal to multiplayer game engines, networking, and spatial interaction.
Weak Python/PyTorch skills relative to position demands; would require rapid ramp-up.
No prior robotics or speech-interaction evaluation experience.
Postdoc is 3-year fixed-term; career progression pathway unclear.
MSc completion timeline must align with employment start.
Potential security clearance delays or complications.
